From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>

Subject: Hosted evaluation — compact post-demo recap, endpoints & next actions

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap + the small set of asks we agreed on so we can move your hosted evaluation forward: 

Summary of what we saw today
- Use case: customer-support assistant that summarizes recent tickets & generates suggested responses.
- Typical request size: ~120 tokens of user + 80 tokens of system/prompt.
- Expected steady-state: ~8–12 req/s; peak bursts up to ~30 req/s during business hours.
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for the chat endpoint.
- Data residency: must remain in US (no EU region storage).

Your asks we flagged on the call
1) Can hosted meet the throughput + p95 latency target for your peak profile?
2) How does rate limiting/bursting work on hosted? Can you test with our real traffic pattern?
3) Is there an option to reserve capacity (Dedicated) later if hosted can't meet sustained peaks?
4) What are the recommended endpoints mapping for our flow (single-turn vs multi-turn, embeddings for search)?
5) Sandbox access for end-to-end validation + a short canary run.

Immediate next steps (what we'll do)
- I attached the session profile CSV and the requirements PDF you shared in the call. We'll load the profile into our perf team for an initial throughput check (ETA 48 hours).
- Provision a sandbox API key (50k tokens/day, two-week window) so you can run your end-to-end flows — Dylan will prog this.
- I sketched recommended endpoint mappings below; we can formalize in a short SE session: /v1/chat -> multi-turn assistant, /v1/generate -> single-turn generation, /v1/embeddings -> semantic search.
- Hosted rate limiting: default quota is token and RPS based. We can temporarily increase burst caps for the sandbox and submit a formal rate review for production.

Action items for you
- Please send a short traffic profile file (minute-level counts for a representative weekday and weekend) if you can — that helps with batching/kv-cache sizing.
- Confirm retention requirement beyond 30 days, if any (for audit/compliance).

Proposed times for SE deep-dive (30-45 min)
- Wed 12/08 10:00–10:45am ET or Thu 12/09 2:00–2:45pm ET. Let me know what works.

Attachments: CloudTailor_Session_Profile.csv, CloudTailor_Requirements_v1.pdf (attached as stubs).

Thanks — I’ll follow up here once the perf run is back.

—

On Tue, Dec 7, 2026 at 9:04 AM Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cloudtailor.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Ava — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side:
> - Burst behavior: our traffic is spiky (support opens at 9am) and we need short bursts up to ~30 req/s for 2–5 minutes. Is that something hosted handles without request drops?
> - Pricing: is it strictly token-based or are there RPS tiers we should expect?
> - Future pivot: if hosted looks good in the two-week pilot but cannot meet sustained peaks, we'd want a path to reserved capacity (dedicated). Is that a standard migration?

Short answers: yes/mostly/yes — longer below.

Bursting and rate limits
- Hosted: we enforce per-key RPS caps plus token quotas. Small short bursts (like 2–5 minutes at 30 rps) are usually absorbed by our burst buffer if within quota; sustained bursts require a quota increase. For the sandbox we can bump your burst cap to 50 rps for limited windows.

Pricing
- Primary billing is token-based. There are optional committed tiers (Reserved/Dedicated) for predictable unit economics where you commit to spend and get a lower per-token rate + guaranteed throughput.

Migration path to Dedicated
- Standard flow: pilot on Hosted -> qualify throughput in sandbox -> if sustained peaks exceed hosted economics, migrate to Dedicated (reserved pools). We assist with model pinning and traffic routing to make the cutover seamless.

Endpoint mapping (suggested)
- /v1/chat : multi-turn assistant + kv/prefix cache to keep context cheap. Good for your ticket-conversation flows.
- /v1/generate : one-off templated generations (subject lines, canned responses).
- /v1/embeddings : vector search for prior tickets; recommend batching embeddings when ingesting historical data.

Operational notes
- Prefix/KV cache: for session-based flows we recommend a small prefix cache per user (reduces repeated token costs when context re-uses).
- Canary plan: start with 10% traffic to Hosted chat endpoint, 50 rps cap, monitor latencies & error rates for 48 hours; increase to 100% if SLOs met.

I'll loop Dylan on provisioning the sandbox and scheduling the SE deep-dive. Thanks for the traffic CSV — that helps us pick initial batching params.

Links for reference: HubSpot deal(RDW-2026-CT-0042) and a doc with our production gating checklist.

—
Ava

Thanks — I can take the SE deep-dive and will own sandbox provisioning. Quick ops checklist and notes before we talk: 

What I will provision now
- Sandbox API key (scoped): 50k tokens/day, burst cap bumped to 50 rps for the first 7 days; default logging retained for 14 days.
- A short runbook (sandbox-instructions.md) attached with curl examples and a small Python snippet for KV cache hints.

SE deep-dive agenda (30–45 min)
1) Review minute-level CSV you sent and confirm expected burst windows.
2) Map core flows to endpoints and pick default model variants for cost/latency tradeoffs.
3) Validate prefix/KV cache sizing and expected per-user token delta.
4) Walk through canary routing & fallback (hosted -> smaller model or fall back to cached summary).

Operational proposal (canary)
- Phase 1: 10% traffic to Hosted chat endpoint, 50 rps cap, monitor p95 latency & 5xx rates for 48h.
- Phase 2: If p95 < 300ms and error rate < 0.5%, increase to 50% and run another 48h.
- Phase 3: Flip to 100% or open conversation about Dedicated if sustained > 60 rps is needed.

Action items for CloudTailor
- Confirm which timezone your team prefers for the deep-dive (Ava suggested Wed 12/08 10am ET).
- Share any retention or encryption/KMS constraints beyond standard US residency.

I’ll provision the sandbox now and post the API key here (or send to the email you prefer).
